f.title: Apply ICH E2/E6 AE reporting to paediatric studies using age-appropriate normal values
f.statement: The ICH E2 guidances and ICH E6, which describe adverse event reporting, apply to pediatric studies. Age-appropriate normal laboratory values and clinical measurements should be used in adverse event reporting.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: ICH guidances on E2 topics and ICH E6, which describe adverse event reporting, apply to pediatric studies. Age-appropriate, normal laboratory values and clinical measurements should be used in adverse event reporting.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 84 because quote proves statement; actor not named in the quote (sponsor/applicant inferred).

f.title: Consider long-term studies or surveillance for effects on growth, maturation and development
f.statement: Because growth and development may not manifest an adverse event acutely but at a later stage of growth and maturation, long-term studies or surveillance data, either while patients are on chronic therapy or during the post-therapy period, may be needed to determine possible effects on skeletal, behavioral, cognitive, sexual and immune maturation and development.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote: In addition, the dynamic processes of growth and development may not manifest an adverse event acutely, but at a later stage of growth and maturation. Long-term studies or surveillance data, either while patients are on chronic therapy or during the posttherapy period, may be needed to determine possible effects on skeletal, behavioral, cognitive, sexual, and immune maturation and development.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 72 because 'may be needed' - Recommended level is a judgement call; actor not named in the quote (sponsor/applicant inferred).

f.title: Conduct postmarketing surveillance and, where needed, long-term follow-up in paediatric patients
f.statement: Because the pediatric database is normally limited at the time of approval, postmarketing surveillance is particularly important. In some cases, long-term follow-up studies may be important to determine effects of certain medications on growth and development of pediatric patients.
f.applicability: Medicinal products used in the pediatric population

rows.quote: Normally the pediatric database is limited at the time of approval. Therefore, postmarketing surveillance is particularly important. In some cases, long-term follow-up studies may be important to determine effects of certain medications on growth and development of pediatric patients.

f.title: Anticipate and reduce known hazards; investigators to know all relevant toxicity before study start
f.statement: Every effort should be made to anticipate and reduce known hazards in pediatric studies. Investigators should be fully aware, before the start of a clinical study, of all relevant preclinical and clinical toxicity of the medicinal product.

rows.deadline: Before the start of the clinical study

f.title: Ensure paediatric study staff are trained to evaluate and manage paediatric adverse events
f.statement: To minimize risk in pediatric clinical studies, those conducting the study should be properly trained and experienced in studying the pediatric population, including the evaluation and management of potential pediatric adverse events.

rows.actor: Those conducting the study (investigators and study staff)
rows.quote: To minimize risk in pediatric clinical studies, those conducting the study should be properly trained and experienced in studying the pediatric population, including the evaluation and management of potential pediatric adverse events.

f.title: Have mechanisms to terminate a paediatric study rapidly if an unexpected hazard is noted
f.statement: Mechanisms should be in place to ensure that a study can be rapidly terminated should an unexpected hazard be noted.

rows.quote: Mechanisms should be in place to ensure that a study can be rapidly terminated should an unexpected hazard be noted.

f.title: Use safety and risk considerations to decide on risk mitigation such as staggered enrolment by age
f.statement: Safety and risk considerations based on existing knowledge should guide the decision whether specific risk mitigation, such as staggered enrollment based on age group, is necessary in a pediatric development program.
f.clause: Addendum 5.1 The Use of Existing Knowledge in Pediatric Drug Development
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Risk management & minimisation

f.title: Collect additional paediatric safety data even when efficacy is extrapolated
f.statement: When efficacy in the pediatric population can be extrapolated from data obtained in the reference populations, leveraging of safety data from the reference to the pediatric population may be utilized; however, additional pediatric safety data are usually required, as existing data may only provide some information about potential safety concerns related to the use of a drug in the pediatric population.
f.clause: Addendum 5.1.1 The Use of Extrapolation in Pediatric Drug Development
f.applicability: Pediatric programmes using extrapolation of efficacy
f.exceptions: Safety data from the reference population may be leveraged.

rows.quote: When efficacy in the pediatric population can be extrapolated from data obtained in the reference populations, leveraging of safety data from the reference to the pediatric population may be utilized; however, additional pediatric safety data are usually required, as existing data may only provide some information about potential safety concerns related to the use of a drug in the pediatric population [See ICH E11 (2000) Section 2.4].

f.title: Use planned safety data collection to design paediatric studies and paediatric pharmacovigilance activities
f.statement: Planned collection of safety data in nonclinical studies, adult clinical studies regardless of dose or indication, or information from other sources (e.g., M&S), should serve to improve the design of pediatric studies and pharmacovigilance activities to address specific pediatric safety concerns.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Risk management & minimisation

f.title: Plan baseline and regular follow-up assessments of growth, development and organ function and discuss with regulators
f.statement: Long-term effects of drug treatment in children can include impacts on development, growth and/or maturation of organ/system function. Therefore, adequate baseline assessments of growth/development and organ function, and regular follow-up measurements, should be planned and discussed with regulatory authorities, as appropriate.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Address dose accuracy, stability, bioavailability and safety when adult preparations must be modified for children
f.statement: When modifications of the available (adult) preparations for pediatric use are unavoidable, measures to minimize the impact on dose accuracy, stability, bioavailability and safety must be addressed.
f.applicability: Pediatric use requiring modification of available preparations
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Clinical safety monitoring
